observed_result.summary: Two unlocked runs against the real store (one CTK identity each, created and deleted under owner decision D4) and no lock run. Current unlocked-row evidence is the v3 run (probe v3, 2026-10-31T20:09:28Z, launchd Aqua session, macOS 27.0.1 26A434, screen unlocked in 3/3 samples; probe exit 1). Passed: create (rc 0, no prompt); non-exportable (export wrote no file and printed 'hardware bounded and cannot be exported', but sc_auth exited 0); delete by exact hash with the identity list equal to the pre-run list; dedicated-agent signing (the key loaded only through ssh-add -K -S as ECDSA-SK, ownership proven by the EC-point hash and by a fingerprint equal to sc_auth's SSH hash; PKCS#11 ssh-add -s loaded nothing; the agent signed in every check and 3/3 samples); fresh certificate login to fixture ca1 through the dedicated agent (setup check and 3/3 samples rc 0, 4 'Accepted publickey ... ECDSA-SK-CERT' lines in ca1's log with the agent key's fingerprint) while the ca2 principal-mismatch and ca1-without-agent controls were refused (both rc 255). Failed: the KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES limit (a random non-matching hash still loaded one key), reproducing v1. After delete-ctk-identity the agent still listed the key but could not sign (ssh-add -T rc 1, -Y sign rc 255). Cleanup complete (probe record: identity list equal to the pre-run list, AuthenticationAuthority unchanged; the orchestrator reports 0 identities listed afterwards). The v1 run (2026-10-09, Background session, macOS 27.0 26A428) gave the same results for create, export, delete, signing, the limit clause and the after-delete check; its fixture login was unmeasured because of a v1 client-config defect that v3 fixes (rows.unlocked.earlier_runs keeps its data). U3_keychain_certificates_limit.inference: Reproduced: a non-matching KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES again did not stop ssh-add -K -S from loading a key. The key was presumably this run's identity: the store held no other CTK identity (pre-run count 0) and the log reports no smart card or token (security list-smartcards rc 44, run.log). With other ecdsa256 identities present (CTK identities, smart cards, other tokens; ssh-keychain(8)), ssh-add -K -S would presumably load them all, so Heimdall cannot rely on KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES for selection. Not tested: whether the variable is read at all on this path (a single-identity store cannot show it), and behaviour with two or more identities, which would need a second CTK identity.

Requirement IDs are for traceability of the lock row only; this record is not by itself evidence that a requirement is met.

One CTK identity was created and deleted in the owner's real user token store in each of two runs: v1 on 2026-10-09 and v3 on 2026-10-31. Each run found the store empty before (pre-run identity count 0, probe-reported) and its identity list equal to the pre-run list afterwards (probe-reported SHA-256 comparison). The owner's identities (none) were counted, never listed into artifacts.

Disclosure, D4 coverage: the v1 record's blocked_on said that a v3 run against the real store creates another CTK identity and therefore needs confirmation that D4 covers it. The orchestrator ran the v3 unlocked run on 2026-10-31 relying on progress.md ('The next real-store run creates and deletes one more identity under D4') and without that confirmation. The identity was deleted by its exact hash, and the store matches the pre-run state (probe-reported; the orchestrator reports 0 identities listed afterwards). Open owner question: does D4 cover further real-store runs, including the lock run?

Session: the v1 run executed from the launchd Background session of an agent process, the v3 run from an Aqua session (launchctl managername, run record); neither used a Heimdall signer. A Heimdall signer as a LaunchAgent or daemon, and a context with no GUI login, were not measured. In the v1 Background session the Docker credential helper could not reach the login keychain ('current session does not allow user interaction'; transcribed in fixture-20261009T053213Z/NOTE-bring-up.txt); CTK creation, loading and signing did not need it.
Only -t none (no per-use Touch ID) and only p-256-ne. A -t bio identity, an exportable identity, logout, sleep, reboot and headless operation are not measured.

Fixture login (v3) is measured for one certificate variant: a default-extension certificate (principal p-host1, -V -1m:+10m) for a key held in the dedicated agent, on ca1, in the setup check and 3 samples with the screen unlocked. The no-touch-required variant was not needed and not issued. The user-presence flag of the signature was not observed; that it was set is an inference from sshd accepting the certificate without no-touch-required (the fixture config sets no PubkeyAuthOptions). Using the CTK key as the CA key (ssh-keygen -s with an sk key), login after the delete, and login across a lock are not tested.

KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES (U3): both runs had a single CTK identity and no smart card in the store, so the key the control loaded was presumably the run's own identity. The control's key fingerprint is not recorded in either run (the probe keeps no raw output of a control that loaded keys). A single-identity store cannot show whether the variable is read at all or what happens with two or more identities; that would need a second CTK identity and was not done.
The two runs used different OS builds (v1 macOS 27.0 26A428, v3 macOS 27.0.1 26A434); results that agree across them are observations on these two builds only.

The export password was random, single-use and protected nothing; sc_auth accepts it only as an argument, so it was visible to same-user processes for that one command in each run. It was never written anywhere.

sc_auth export-ctk-identity exited 0 while refusing, in both runs. Non-exportability rests on the refusal message, the absence of an output file, and Apple's statement that -ne keys never leave the Secure Enclave (sc_auth(8)); no attempt was made to extract key material by other means.

'No prompt' means nothing blocked with stdin /dev/null and askpass forced to /usr/bin/true; a non-blocking notification on the owner's screen would not be visible to the probe, and no owner attestation was collected in either run (owner_attestation not_asked in the v3 run record). The AuthenticationAuthority digest check detects an accepted SmartCard pairing.

Redaction: the v1 identity row's local time of day was redacted after the run (20261009T053616Z-unlocked/REDACTION.txt; macOS separates it from AM/PM with U+202F). The v3 run redacts it in-run (identity-row.txt shows '<local-time>').

For the v3 run, the fixture logs, the self-test log as captured by the orchestrator and a post-run check (0 CTK identities, 0 fixture containers, taken about 10 minutes after the run) were added afterwards under tests/evidence/artifacts/g04/p5/20261031T200928Z-unlocked/orchestrator/; the self-test's exit status was 0.
The v3 run record self-reports status verified / verdict fail and build_commit null, with empty requirement_ids; this record takes its status from the lowest-row rule and states build_commit above.
Lock row: not executed. The self-test's fake sc_auth and the software-key rehearsals never count as CTK or lock evidence.
2026-10-31: ADR-0004 §2 answered the D4 question (further real-store runs are covered, each creating and deleting one CTK identity); this also covers the v3 run of that day retroactively.
blocked_on: a screen lock/unlock cycle for the lock row (tests/native/macos/g04_ctk_probe.sh --mode lock, v3). Since 2026-10-31 the orchestrator may lock the screen itself once the console has been idle for at least 15 minutes (ADR-0004 §2); the probe's lock mode needs an automated-lock variant for that, or the owner at the console. D4 covers further real-store runs, including the lock run (ADR-0004 §2). The unlocked row needs no further real-store run: its login clause was measured in the v3 run on 2026-10-31.
